questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Good opportunities for studying and meeting new people, seeing great places and learning all at the same time.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: This six months has been the best time ever, if you have the opportunity to go on exchange, then do it!! :))

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, the international student office will email all info.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: You will get most information before arrival or at orientation week, even though i've found the orientation a bit repetitive from the email info.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: it was nice and easy

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I can be a bit tricky but i would really recommend giving it a shot on sites such as facebook, flatmates, realestate sites for short term leases etc. The housing from what i have been told by other students on campus is expensive and not the best facilities

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived in scarborough with to other danish people. i had the best time ever even though it takes some time to get to uni. but you are right by scarborough beach which is amazing in spring and summer!!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: mentioned aboved

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: pretty easy, the international student office will contact you when they need action from you when it comes to units and registration

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: pretty good - i got all the units i applied for.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Again, the internation student office will help you with any matter or questions you might have

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: very succesfull since i got all the classes i needed.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: just take the time to research the units if you are eligible for them or if they have certain restrictions, and also if you are looking at an old unit calendar / overview, if they are available for the semester that you are going abroad on.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The course level are easier from my experience than courses at KU. But we had way more assignments and also some mandatory classes.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Different, quite a bit of tests and assignments but these count a percentage of your full grade for the unit, so you dont have to stress that much about the final exam which was nice.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Management and organisations, Social psychology of work, Boodjar Moort Karjijin and Politics of the mass media

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed politics of the mass media, and how political actors use tools to frame and push their agenda.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Groceries can be quite expensive, which was my most unexpected cost, since you spend quite a bit on this.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: public transport and sushi!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: i didn't really use them.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: many different kinds even though i didn't attend.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: go. on. roadtrips. i cant stress it enough. I went to both exmouth and esperance (north and south of western australia) and it was literally the best and most beautiful trips of my life :))

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: shorter trips to mararget river, rottnest island etc.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: pretty easy, australian culture is not that different from back home in my opinion :)

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: This was more a challenge, but mostly since the people in my class were quite young (18-19) and straight out of high school. so most of my friends i made in other exchange students :)

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The layed back energy!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: prepare to have the best time ever!!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: if you can live with the uncertaintly of not knowing your living situration until you get really close to your leave date, then do this. I would really really really recommend to live off campus and go to house viewings when you get to perth.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: meeting so many amazing new people and seeing cool places!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: having to go back!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
